payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_batch.py::test_a_batch_whose_package_raised_closes_infrastructure_whatever_it_stopped_on stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'Only a marked `CellRuntimeError` is promoted, so a marked `PackageError` drains at exit 0.' applied to saffron/batch.py as an edit. The claim was '`run_batch` closes its row `INFRASTRUCTURE`, and returns it, once its runner raised a marked exception, whatever reason the loop stopped on. The loop still runs every later candidate it would have run. The log carries a line naming the command `saffron package <spec id>` for the spec that raised, and for no other spec. That spec keeps its `raised` line beside the command line. A later candidate whose runner raised an unmarked `CellRuntimeError` or `PackageError` gets its `raised` line and no command line. Two marked raises in a row still fire the breaker, so a third candidate never runs. The witness drives each of the four reasons the loop can stop on besides the breaker: `DRAINED`, `BUDGET`, `UNTIL` and `INCOMPLETE`. The `DRAINED` case raises a marked `PackageError` and the other three a marked `CellRuntimeError`.', and only that witness ran under the edit.
